name: Look up a member's savings balance
description: Search Member Services by member ID and branch code, then read the savings balance from the member detail panel. Read-only.

parameters.name: member_id
parameters.description: The member's identifier, as printed on their statement.

parameters.name: branch_code
parameters.description: Three-digit branch code the lookup is scoped to.

outputs.name: savings_balance
outputs.description: The savings balance as displayed, including currency formatting.

steps.description: Open the Member Services search screen.

checkpoint.description: the Member Services search form is loaded

steps.description: Type the member ID into the Member ID field.

target.robustness_note: Rung 1 holds because this field carries a real aria-label, so it survives restyling and DOM churn. If the label is renamed per tenant, rung 2 re-anchors on the visible 'Member ID' caption in the adjacent cell. Rung 3 assumes this is the first textbox on the page and breaks if a field is inserted above it. Coordinates are last resort and viewport-bound.
Same rung-1 identification as the step itself; the checkpoint only has to confirm the value landed.

checkpoint.description: the Member ID field holds the supplied member ID

steps.description: Type the branch code into the unlabelled Branch Code field.

target.robustness_note: THIS LADDER STARTS AT RUNG 2 BY NECESSITY: the field has no label element, no id and no aria-label, so it is anonymous in the accessibility tree and rung 1 does not exist for it. Rung 2 anchors on the visible 'Branch Code' caption and takes the textbox sharing its row, which survives restyling and column reordering. Rung 3 assumes it is the second textbox on the page. Coordinates last.
Re-resolves the anonymous field the same way the step did, so the checkpoint cannot pass by reading a different field.

checkpoint.description: the Branch Code field holds the supplied branch code

target.robustness_note: A real <button> with a stable accessible name, so rung 1 is safe. Rung 2 anchors on the search form's last caption rather than the button's own text, which covers a relabel to 'Find' or 'Go' — the one change that would break rung 1.

checkpoint.description: the search returned a response: either a member detail panel or an alert

steps.description: Read the savings balance from the member detail panel.

target.robustness_note: Rung 1 is name-only on purpose. The value span carries aria-label 'Savings Balance', and the accessibility tree also hands that name to the enclosing table cell, so role+name matches two elements and is ambiguous while name alone is exact. Rung 2 is the honest fallback for this legacy table: take the row whose caption cell reads 'Savings Balance' and read its second cell. Rung 2 also survives the aria-label being dropped entirely, which is the likeliest drift here.

checkpoint.description: the member detail panel is displayed, so the value read belongs to this member

known_outcomes.name: balance_returned
known_outcomes.message: Member detail panel rendered; the savings balance was read.

known_outcomes.name: member_not_found
known_outcomes.message: No member exists with that ID. A legitimate answer to return, not a failure.

known_outcomes.name: permission_denied
known_outcomes.message: The member exists but the operating account may not view it.

known_outcomes.name: member_id_not_submitted
known_outcomes.message: The app reports an empty Member ID, so our type step did not take effect. Our bug, not the caller's answer.

known_outcomes.name: branch_code_not_submitted
known_outcomes.message: The app reports an empty Branch Code, so the rung-2 resolution typed into the wrong field or none at all.

dismiss_target.robustness_note: A real button with a stable name; an interstitial this simple needs no fallback rung.

provenance.approved_by: hand-written for the M1 schema checkpoint, corrected against the real app in M0
